According to the latest issue of the Power On newsletter, Apple is reportedly once considered adding a feature to the Apple Upgrade programme that would make iPhone setup almost seamless: having your data copied to your new device by Apple in advance. However, this feature never saw the light of day.

The concept is simple: since users upgrade their devices periodically through fixed monthly instalments, why not make the process of switching to a new phone as easy as possible? Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman reported as follows:

There are clearly some loopholes here. First, your iCloud backup will be slightly out of date, because the data transfer can only take place when the device is shipped, which will lag by a few days — unless you choose to pick it up in store.

In addition, there are obvious privacy concerns. That said, if you've always been backing up to iCloud, the fact that Apple has your data shouldn't be surprising in itself. But for the general public, there may be concerns about how the data is transferred to the new phone, and whether anyone might have peeked at the data during the process.

Two years ago, Apple launched a brand-new "Presto" system at its retail stores, allowing staff to update the system of an iPhone while it was still in its packaging. One can imagine that this system could be extended in the future to support iCloud backup transfers, and the whole process wouldn't require anyone to touch your data.

Nonetheless, this feature was ultimately not rolled out, and this outcome may be a good thing.
